key_insight: Structurally distinct Y6 aggregates enable ultrafast energy transfer that supports efficient charge generation in organic homojunction solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Engineering aggregate packing and complementary charge-transfer character could improve organic solar cells without conventional donor–acceptor bulk heterojunctions.
method: Probe Y6 aggregate dynamics using ultrafast spectroscopy.
Identify inter-aggregate Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET).
Develop a multi-component FRET framework linking aggregation, charge-transfer character, and excited-state dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 65% ensemble-averaged FRET efficiency on a sub-picosecond timescale (<1 ps), linking this pathway to long-range energy migration and high external quantum efficiency.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify device-efficiency gains from controlled aggregate engineering or establish generality beyond Y6.
paper_title: Ultrafast Inter-Aggregate Energy Transfer Drives Efficient Charge Generation in Organic Homojunctions
